maria.lopez: Heads up — Helix (enterprise POC) just sent final traffic profile. They expect 100 sustained qps, 250 qps 5–10m burst windows, avg seq len ~600 tokens, occasional long tails to 2k. Asking: recommended reserved GPUs for commit, autoscale/burst policy, KV-cache warmup strategy, and delta on monthly cost if they buy reserved vs relying on burst credits. Also some security Qs re: KMS/HSM and audit logs.

samir.patel: quick Q — mix of calls? generation vs embeddings vs rerank?

maria.lopez: Mostly text generation (~85%), small percentage embeddings for similarity (~10%), rerank ~5%. No streaming needed for first phase.

alex.chen: okay. For 100 sustained qps w/ avg 600 tokens, rough tokens/sec = 100 * 600 / 1 = 60k tokens/sec? wait math — we usually size on tokens/min. Better to share requests/sec * avg latency in seconds. can you add target p50/p95 latency SLO?

maria.lopez: SLO = p95 < 500ms for interactive endpoints. Batch window allowed for background jobs.

jordan.wright: p95 <500ms with 600 token avg will need model shard sizing. If they accept 8-bit quantized variants we can fit more streams per GPU. For a safe reserved commit I'd recommend reserving 4x A100-like GPUs (or equivalent capacity) with burst pool of +2 GPUs for short windows. That gives headroom for preheat and minor spikes.

samir.patel: agree. Also propose autoscale policy: keep min_instances = 4 (reserved), burst_policy = {"max_additional": 2, "burst_window_minutes": 15, "cooldown": 10}. If they want longer bursts we price accordingly.

alex.chen: pricing delta: ballpark — reserved 4 GPUs committed monthly vs pure burst credits. Committed cost ~60% of on-demand for same capacity; burst credits billed at on-demand rates with small markup. I'll pull numbers from quote deck but estimate ~1.6x cost for relying mostly on burst for same availability.

maria.lopez: good. Helix also asked about KV-cache warmup — they worry about first-request latency.

jordan.wright: KV-cache warmup approach: synthetic prefix warmup from a representative prompt set. We can run a preheat job to populate per-shard KV caches. Example priming job (one-off) — run on preheat node:

```
# curl warmup list (example)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '{"model": "redwood-quant-8b", "prompts": ["<sample prompt 1>", "<sample prompt 2>"]}'
```

jordan.wright: we also support `prefill_kv=true` in the preheat workflow to mark the cache as warm for routing. That reduces p95 for first real user request.

samir.patel: operational note — schedule preheat 10–15m before planned marketing pushes. For continued KV effectiveness, include periodic light heartbeat requests.

eden.park: security notes — for enterprise commit, Helix wants KMS integration + monthly audit logs retention. We support customer KMS and HSM via Private deployment or Dedicated with KMS passthrough. Need to confirm whether they require FIPS/TLS-only endpoints and whether PIIs are stored. Also send them our standard security questionnaire addendum for Dedicated.

maria.lopez: flagged — I will attach questionnaire. Eden, can you list 3 must-have items we should confirm before commit?

eden.park: 1) KMS key ownership and rotation policy (customer-managed)
2) Audit log retention window + S3 export capability
3) Data-in-transit and at-rest encryption proofs (certs)

alex.chen: one more thing — mention fallback model variants. Recommend setting routing fallback to a cheaper quantized model if burst capacity exhausted; keeps app online with slightly degraded quality. We can include A/B rollout plan in contract.

maria.lopez: perfect. Helix also asked whether reserved GPUs can be region-affine (we prefer us-west2).

jordan.wright: yes. We can pin AZ/region for Dedicated pools; preheat must run in same region for KV affinity. If they need multi-AZ resilience, add cross-AZ fallback nodes (adds ~10% to commit cost).

deploy-bot: preheat-job scheduled for helix-poc -> job_id=preheat-3432101111, eta 2024-11-05T09:10:00Z :white_check_mark:

maria.lopez: next actions: (1) Helix to send per-endpoint RPS and sample prompt set (seq length histogram). (2) Alex to attach cost delta estimate and sample contract clause for burst credits. (3) Eden to attach security addendum. (4) We'll schedule a 30m call Thurs to align on commit size. I'll send invites. :thumbsup:

samir.patel: lgtm

alex.chen: sending numbers in 30m

jordan.wright: will prepare preheat checklist and automated warmup script

eden.park: prepping security addendum

maria.lopez: thanks team — keeping this thread for audit.
